# How are malignant and immune compartments spatially organized across two HNSCC tissue sections? {.hero-title}

This project combines sample-level Seurat analysis, reciprocal PCA integration and SpaCET deconvolution to describe spatial transcriptional domains and sample-relative immune niches in two 10x Genomics Visium sections.

::: {.hero-actions}
[Explore results](results.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg}
[Review methods](methods.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-lg}
[Read the scientific report](reports/HNSCC_spatial_transcriptomics_report.html){.btn .btn-outline-secondary .btn-lg}
:::
:::

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Scope at a glance

The project contains **two biological samples**. Cross-sample comparisons are descriptive, spots within each section are not independent biological replicates, and SpaCET fractions are transcriptional estimates rather than exact cell counts.
:::

## Project at a glance

::: {.grid .glance-grid}
::: {.card .feature-card}
::: {.card-body}
### 2 tissue sections

HNSCC Visium samples **17B5776** and **19H1257**, analyzed independently before joint comparison.
:::
:::

::: {.card .feature-card}
::: {.card-body}
### 4 analysis stages

Quality control, individual clustering, RPCA integration and spatial deconvolution.
:::
:::

::: {.card .feature-card}
::: {.card-body}
### Sample-relative niches

Immune-high and Immune-low spots are defined from quartiles calculated separately within each section.
:::
:::

::: {.card .feature-card}
::: {.card-body}
### Reproducible outputs

Saved objects, marker tables, SpaCET summaries, spatial figures and a scientific report support the portfolio narrative.
:::
:::
:::

## Computational workflow

::: {.workflow-grid}
::: {.workflow-step}
<span class="step-number">01</span>

### Import and QC

Load Space Ranger counts and tissue coordinates; inspect spot-level transcript, feature and mitochondrial metrics.
:::

::: {.workflow-step}
<span class="step-number">02</span>

### Normalize and cluster

Apply SCTransform, PCA, graph-based clustering and marker-guided spatial-domain assessment within each sample.
:::

::: {.workflow-step}
<span class="step-number">03</span>

### Integrate samples

Use a joint representation and RPCA integration to describe shared and sample-associated transcriptional structure.
:::

::: {.workflow-step}
<span class="step-number">04</span>

### Resolve compartments

Use SpaCET to estimate malignant, stromal and immune fractions, then map sample-relative immune niches.
:::
:::

## Selected findings

::: {.grid .finding-grid}
::: {.card .result-card}
![Spatial expression of selected lineage- and state-associated markers in 17B5776.](results/figures/17B5776_spatial_marker_validation.png){.card-img-top .lightbox}

::: {.card-body}
### Spatial transcriptional heterogeneity

**Observation.** Sample 17B5776 contains spatially organized marker programs associated with immune, epithelial, stromal, hypoxic, inflammatory, interferon-responsive and proliferative domains.

**Interpretation.** These are provisional mixed-spot domain annotations, not pure cell types or formally defined malignant states.
:::
:::

::: {.card .result-card}
![Estimated total immune-fraction distributions across the two HNSCC tissue sections.](results/figures/spacet_immune_fraction_distribution.png){.card-img-top .lightbox}

::: {.card-body}
### Contrasting immune distributions

**Observation.** The saved SpaCET summary reports a higher median derived immune fraction in 17B5776 than in 19H1257.

**Interpretation.** This is a descriptive contrast between two sampled sections and cannot be generalized to an HNSCC population.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What remains unresolved

The current workflow characterizes malignant fractions and immune niches, but it does **not** formally identify distinct malignant transcriptional states. Estimated malignant fractions and epithelial marker patterns should not be presented as a completed malignant-state analysis.
:::
